root_cause: The coredns-custom ConfigMap in kube-system overrides DNS resolution with a server block that forwards every query for '.' to the on-prem DNS server 10.20.1.53, which no longer responds. All external lookups hit that dead upstream and time out, while in-cluster names still resolve because they are served by the managed Kubernetes zone rather than the custom block.
evidence: kubectl-get-cm-coredns-custom.yaml: data.Corefile contains a server block for '.' with 'forward . 10.20.1.53'
kubectl-logs-coredns.txt: repeated "read udp ... 10.20.1.53:53: i/o timeout" for api.stripe.com and graph.microsoft.com
nslookup-from-pod.txt: api.stripe.com times out while orders-api.shop.svc.cluster.local resolves to a cluster IP
az-network-vnet-show.json: dhcpOptions.dnsServers is empty, so the VNet uses Azure-provided DNS (red herring)
kubectl-get-pods-kube-system.txt: both CoreDNS pods Running with no restarts (red herring)
fix: Remove the '.' server block from the coredns-custom ConfigMap so CoreDNS falls back to the Azure-provided resolver 168.63.129.16, or point the forward at a working upstream, then let CoreDNS reload.
